title: The Karmapas
hook: the line of the Karmapas, heads of a Kagyu school, recognized life after life

segments.voice: Yesterday: Tsongkhapa and the path in three: renunciation, bodhicitta and right view.

A sealed letter, kept safe by a teacher's closest students after his death. Inside, the stories say, are clues: the name of a valley, the shape of a house, the names of a child's parents. Search parties set out to follow them. Somewhere, a small boy is found, tested, and brought to a monastery, where he is honored as the same teacher, returned. In the Karma Kagyu school, the stories say, this has happened again and again. Today, the Karmapas.
screen: `A SEALED LETTER OF CLUES.` → `A SEARCH PARTY SETS OUT.` → `THE SAME TEACHER, RETURNED.`

segments.voice: First, the line. The Karmapas are the heads of the Karma Kagyu, one of the Kagyu schools that grew from the stream of Marpa, Milarepa and Gampopa. Each Karmapa is recognized as the rebirth of the one before, so the line runs life after life. Second, the word for such a teacher: tulku, a Tibetan word for an emanation body. Tibetan Buddhist teaching holds that an awakened teacher can choose to be reborn, out of compassion, to keep teaching. A tulku is not just a clever child. In the tradition's understanding, it is the same stream of mind taking up its work again. Third, how one is found. Tradition says Karmapas have often left letters describing where they would be reborn, and that senior teachers read the signs, search, and confirm. The child is then raised and trained, sometimes from a very young age, to become the teacher the school believes he already is. The Karmapa is also linked to a black crown, worn in a ceremony that devotees say brings blessing to all who see it. Fourth, honesty about a hard chapter. In recent times, different groups within the tradition have recognized different candidates for the same Karmapa, and that question has caused real pain among practitioners. This lesson takes no side. What stays the same is the idea at the center: a teaching held not only in books, but in a living line of people, passed from hand to hand.
screen: `HEADS OF THE KARMA KAGYU.` · `TULKU: AN EMANATION BODY.` · `LETTERS, SIGNS, A SEARCH.` · `A HARD CHAPTER, NO SIDE TAKEN.` · then, large: `A LIVING LINE OF PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing you know how to do, a recipe, a trade, a prayer, and the person who taught it to you. Then, if you know, ask who taught them, going back one face at a time as far as the line goes, and on the out-breath let a little thanks run back along it.
The Karmapas. The heads of the Karma Kagyu school, each recognized as the rebirth of the one before, a teacher returning life after life. Today's word.
Your line: life after life. The same stream of mind, taking up its work again. Day nine hundred eighty-two, done.

howItsDone: In the Karma Kagyu school, the Karmapa is honored as the head of the lineage; practitioners recite lineage prayers naming past Karmapas, and recognized tulkus are trained from childhood by senior teachers.
